title: MRC Impact Acceleration Awards
purpose: Support a single high-risk development step for a new or repurposed medicine, medical device, diagnostic or other medical intervention. The project should generate critical data that de-risks further development.
eligibility: Project lead must be based at an MRC-eligible research organisation, direct the project and be actively involved. Only one application can be submitted as project lead.
scope: Includes advanced therapeutics such as RNA and nucleic-acid therapies, biologics, medicines, medical devices and other medical interventions. All human diseases are eligible.
development_stage: The concept should already have been explored and normally have supporting data. The proposal must focus on one critical development gap rather than a multi-stage research programme.
funding: £50,000–£300,000 full economic cost. MRC normally funds 80% FEC.
key_requirements: Applicant must identify the single high-risk development step, explain why it matters, define success criteria and show how completing it enables further funding/development or patient benefit.
exclusions: Fundamental or investigative research without a product-development plan; multiple work packages; preliminary concept-data generation; later-stage clinical work.

title: MRC Proof of Concept: Stage One
purpose: Develop and test novel therapeutics, medical devices, diagnostics and other medical interventions across the development pathway.
eligibility: Project lead must be employed by an MRC-eligible research organisation, direct the project and actively participate in the work.
scope: Academically led translational research addressing significant health needs. Projects can range from early prototype development through preclinical refinement and testing to early-phase clinical studies up to phase 2a.
development_stage: Sufficient proof-of-concept data must already support the proposed approach.
funding: No fixed maximum specified in the supplied information. Requested resources must be justified. MRC normally funds 80% FEC.
duration: No fixed maximum specified in the supplied information. Duration must be justified according to the proposed work.
key_requirements: Research needs a credible translational pathway toward a medical intervention rather than simply investigating an interesting scientific question.
exclusions: Fundamental or investigative research without a development plan; technology development without a medical or clinical development pathway; late-phase clinical trials; interventions primarily concerned with healthcare-service delivery.

title: Wellcome Discovery Awards
purpose: Support established researchers pursuing bold and creative research capable of creating significant shifts in understanding related to human life, health and wellbeing.
eligibility: Lead applicant must be an established researcher with international standing, experience leading innovative research and a track record of managing and training others. Eligible administering organisations include UK higher-education institutions.
scope: Research can come from any discipline but must either generate a significant shift in understanding or develop methodologies, tools, techniques or frameworks that could benefit health-related research.
development_stage: Discovery research; no specific translational or product-development stage is required.
funding: Applicants request the resources required for the programme. Average award approximately £3.5 million. Applications above £5 million receive additional scrutiny.
duration: Up to 8 years; average approximately 7 years.
deadline: No fixed deadline; applications can currently be submitted at any time.
key_requirements: Research must have potential to improve human life, health or wellbeing. Competitive proposals should be bold, creative, high quality, evidence-supported and capable of producing a substantial advance in understanding or methodology.
exclusions: None specified in the supplied information.

title: Bioinformatics and Biological Resources Fund
funder: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC), UKRI
purpose: Develop, improve or consolidate bioinformatics or biological resources for the wider UK bioscience community.
eligibility: Applicants must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for BBSRC funding.
scope: Projects must deliver a community resource addressing significant demand or serving an established bioscience user base. Examples include shared datasets, bioinformatics resources, software tools and biological collections.
development_stage: Not specified in the supplied information.
funding: Up to £2 million FEC, with BBSRC funding 80%, up to £1.6 million.
key_requirements: Proposed resource should serve a broader research community rather than only the applicant's lab, and applicants must consider its long-term sustainability.
exclusions: Projects primarily focused on biomedical, clinical or healthcare research; answering a specific research hypothesis; generating a new dataset; creating an institution-only resource.
